thread:
deploy-bot: Deploy started for model v31.2 to prod (canary->100%) at 2026-03-15T19:10:00Z. Rollout ID: r-20260315-3712. Watching KPIs :eyes:

Sylvia: getting alerts — GPU pool 'eu-west-pool-7' memory at 97%, queue length spiking, latency p95 climbing. Seeing repeated OOM-ish logs from runtime: `kv_cache_eviction=rare, ctx_len=avg:5.6k -> 12k`

Kevin: paging oncall — I'm on it. Paging details: high latency, 503s for ~2% of requests. Customer error reports coming in. :rotating_light:

incident-bot: Incident created: INCIDENT-20260315-3712 - GPU saturation during v31.2 rollout. Severity P1. Linked runbook: https://internal/runbooks/gpu-saturation

Sylvia: quick snapshot:
- pool: eu-west-pool-7
- affected model: v31.2-full (uses extended ctx prefill)
- GPU mem: 98.7% avg
- queue length: 312 -> 1,200 in 7m
- error type: throttle / 503 from worker pool
- KV-cache size per-shard: +3x after canary -> sustained growth

Maria: initial hypothesis — v31.2 changed tokenizer/context handling, increasing prefix lengths and kv-cache retention. That increases per-request GPU mem and IO for kv lookups. Autoscaler is hitting max-replicas (quota 48) and cannot provision more ephemeral GPU nodes fast enough.

Oliver: confirmed autoscaler errors in controller logs:
```
E03015 19:12:43 autoscaler controller: desiredReplicas=120 current=48 quotaExceeded=true
E03015 19:12:44 provider api: insufficient capacity in eu-west-zone-b
```

Nav: customer-facing impact: a subset of heavy-context customers (chatbots, long-document summarizers) experiencing timeouts and 503s. CS queue tripled. I'll notify top 10 customers and escalate SLAs.

Kevin: immediate mitigations in flight (status updates):
1) Redirect 30% of traffic for v31.2 -> v30.9 (stable smaller-ctx variant) via routing policy. Command:
```
redwood route update --model v31.2 --fallback v30.9 --pct 30
```
2) Disable canary->100% rollout to pause further ramping:
```
deploy-bot rollback --id r-20260315-3712 --to canary
```
3) Force eviction of large KV entries older than 24h on affected shards (experimental):
```
runtime-cli kv-evict --pool eu-west-pool-7 --age 24h
```
4) Opened emergency request to cloud provider for extra GPU quota in eu-west-zone-b (already pending).

deploy-bot: Rollout paused at 30% by request of SRE. Canary remains healthy, full rollout frozen.

Sylvia: after routing 30% away, queue dropped from 1,200 -> 540, GPU mem pressure eased to ~92% on split workers. But autoscaler still refusing more replicas because provider region returning capacity errors.

Maria: we observed that v31.2 increased KV cache retention factor and also changed prefill strategy (prefetching entire conversation history). That multiplied GPU working set by ~2.8x for some requests. Preliminary repro on staging with long-history prompts shows same pattern.

Oliver: short-term decision options:
- rollback v31.2 entirely (fast but loses features)
- keep paused rollout and increase fallback routing to v30.9 while we patch prefill logic
- attempt emergency scale to another region and failover traffic (cold, cross-region latency)

Kevin: voted to increase fallback routing to 70% immediately and open rollback as contingency. Executing now.

deploy-bot: routing updated: v31.2 -> v30.9 fallback 70% (effective at 19:18:30Z).

Sylvia: immediate customer impact metrics after fallback bump:
- 503s down from 2% -> 0.4%
- p95 latency returned near baseline for non-heavy-context users
- heavy-context customers still seeing elevated latency (we're isolating by label: ctx>8k tokens)

CS-bot: Notifying top-10 customers via templated message. Template: "We're seeing elevated latency for long-context workloads; we've routed traffic to a stable variant and are working on a patch. ETA preliminary fix 6-12 hrs."

Maria: mitigation plan for next 12 hours:
- revert aggressive prefetch in v31.2 and cut kv retention window (hotfix branch ready)
- add telemetry to measure per-request kv-cache delta
- synthetic load tests to validate memory profile at scale
- schedule controlled canary with throttled prefetch to measure effect

Nav: preparing customer post-incident comms and timeline. Asking SRE for root-cause bullets and expected ETA for rollback/patch.

Kevin: status update 19:35Z — autoscaler still limited due to provider capacity. We've requested vendor support and temporary repave of some nodes to free resources. Meanwhile fallback routing holding system stable.

Sylvia: followups we need to capture as action items:
- ACTION-1: Maria to cut prefetch in v31.2 and push v31.2-hotfix within 2 hours (assigned)
- ACTION-2: Oliver to open quota/capacity escalation with cloud vendor and track until capacity increases or region failover options available
- ACTION-3: Kevin to run a post-incident load test simulating long-history requests against hotfix before re-enable rollout
- ACTION-4: CS to send interim update to affected customers (Nav)

Maria: pushing hotfix to canary now (v31.2-hotfix). Deploying to single shard to validate reduced kv retention.

deploy-bot: v31.2-hotfix canary deployed to shard eu-west-pool-7-01 at 19:46:10Z. Telemetry baseline enabled.

Sylvia: early numbers from hotfix canary after 6m:
- per-request GPU mem down ~42% on sample long-history requests
- KV-cache growth controlled (no sustained 3x growth)
- queue on canary shard stable

Kevin: running canary flood test now (script: scripts/canary_long_history_load.sh) — will validate autoscaler behaviour and confirm we can slowly ramp beyond 30%.

incident-bot: Major incident remains open. Next status in 30m or on major change.

Nav: CS sent interim message to affected customers at 19:55Z. One customer acknowledged, asks for ETA for full fix — replied with 6-12h and offered priority support.

Oliver: recommendation for postmortem — include rollout gating checklist: measure kv-cache delta, simulate long-history traffic during canary, add autoscaler preflight check for estimated GPU working set.

Sylvia: agreed. Also add a short-term policy to default new model rollouts to a conservative prefetch configuration unless explicitly opted-in.

Kevin: closing loop for now — system stable enough with fallback routing and hotfix canary. Will keep incident open until canary scale test passes and we either rollback or resume gradual rollout. Handing off next oncall (Maria) for overnight monitoring.

Maria: taking handoff. I'll post updates every hour or on any regression. :white_check_mark:

CS-bot: Incident update posted to #customers-affected with tag INCIDENT-20260315-3712.

Sylvia: final note to include in postmortem timeline: initial deploy -> 0-7m rapid kv growth -> autoscaler reach quota at ~9m -> routing fallback -> hotfix canary -> stabilization.

-- end of thread --
